extras.name: Install PyTorch on Windows for RTX 5090 / Blackwell (2026 — cu128 is GONE)
extras.note: Do NOT copy old cu128 commands — 2.12 removed them. Use CUDA 13: `pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130`. If your NVIDIA Windows driver is older, fall back to `--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126`. Requires a current Blackwell-capable driver (570+ class minimum for the old 12.8 baseline; newer for CUDA 13). Verify with: `python -c "import torch;print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_capability())"` — you want (12,0) for sm_120. If you see 'no kernel image is available' you have a non-Blackwell build; reinstall from cu130/cu126.

extras.name: torch.compile knobs tuned for single-GPU local inference/diffusion
extras.note: For small-batch local inference: `model = torch.compile(model, mode='reduce-overhead')` (enables CUDA Graphs, kills Python/launch overhead). For a frozen heavy model where compile time is acceptable: `mode='max-autotune'` (CUTLASS/CK GEMM autotuning). First call is slow (warmup/autotune) — exclude it from benchmarks. On Blackwell+Windows, if a Triton FlashAttention kernel fails to build, force `torch.nn.attention.sdpa_kernel` to the cuDNN or mem-efficient backend instead of flash.

extras.name: llama.cpp on Windows: full-VRAM and CPU+GPU offload for 32GB+64GB
extras.note: Download the prebuilt `cudart` + `bin` Windows zips matching your CUDA (12.x or 13.x) — no build needed. Model FITS in 32GB VRAM: `llama-server -m model.Q4_K_M.gguf -ngl 99 --flash-attn --ctx-size 32768 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0` (KV-cache quant frees VRAM for more context). Model BIGGER than 32GB (spill to 64GB RAM): drop -ngl to the layer count that fits (start ~60-80% of layers, watch VRAM), the rest run on CPU. MoE model: keep experts on CPU with `--n-cpu-moe N` (or `--override-tensor 'exps=CPU'`) and put attention/router on GPU — this is the KTransformers-style trick that makes a 40-70GB MoE usable on a 32GB card. Enable 'System Memory Fallback' in the NVIDIA Control Panel for graceful spill.

extras.name: TensorRT-RTX on Windows: install + build an engine from ONNX
extras.note: `pip install tensorrt-rtx` (defaults to CUDA 13.x; use `tensorrt-rtx-cu12` to pin CUDA 12). Export your model to ONNX from PyTorch (`torch.onnx.export` or `torch.onnx.dynamo_export`), then JIT-build an engine at load time — no per-GPU AOT plan file to manage. Use FP8/FP4 or INT8 for Blackwell tensor-core throughput on frozen diffusion/vision models. Best used for a fixed inference graph; do not expect it to handle dynamic training graphs. It's the consumer-RTX product — do NOT reach for datacenter TensorRT or TRT-LLM (TRT-LLM on GeForce is WSL2-only with limited model coverage).

extras.name: Keep the Blackwell trio aligned (the #1 cause of sm_120 failures)
extras.note: The 'sm_120 is not defined for option gpu-name' / 'no kernel image' errors are almost always a PyTorch + Triton + CUDA version mismatch. Rule: PyTorch >= 2.10 pairs with Triton 3.6, and the CUDA runtime must be 12.8+ (ideally CUDA 13 with PyTorch 2.12). Don't mix a cu126 PyTorch with a standalone cu130 Triton. On Windows you get a working Triton bundled inside the PyTorch wheel — avoid hand-installing a separate Triton unless you know you need it.

extras.name: ONNX Runtime install matrix (CUDA EP vs DirectML/WinML on Windows)
extras.note: NVIDIA speed path: `pip install onnxruntime-gpu` (cuda13 variant; chain the TensorRT EP for max perf). Vendor-neutral Windows path (no CUDA dependency, also reaches the Core Ultra iGPU/NPU): the DirectML EP, or the newer WinML which auto-picks the EP (Windows 11 24H2+). DirectML is in sustained engineering — fine for existing apps, but new Windows work should target WinML.

extras.name: PyTorch / CUDA / FlashAttention / Triton / xformers compatibility guide
extras.note: Community-maintained compatibility matrix — handy cross-check when assembling a working PyTorch+CUDA+Triton+FlashAttention+xformers+bitsandbytes set on Blackwell. Verify versions against official release notes before trusting.
